The response is a narrower and more careful framing of the same record, which improves precision but does not cure the underlying compliance gap. The key distinction is proportionality: a narrowed, caveated position can justify moving from an overbroad clean-certification claim to a more limited claim only when the remaining caveat is not itself an unresolved compliance predicate. Here, the caveat is exactly the unresolved predicate. The policy text says materiality is triggered when a weakness affects a named launch use case, and the available record says this segment is named while legal review on disclosure is still open. On that record, aggregate pass results, clean rehearsal severity, public governance guidance, residual-risk notation, and monitoring can support readiness context, but they cannot independently establish policy compliance for certification now. The actor's restraint is analytically better than the original overreach, but it is still not enough to reach compliant_with_caveats from admissible evidence alone.
